sections.name: File setup, flat, attack, block
sections.title: Test setup and synthetic distributions
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the chase win model and its outcome types, and the option functions. Defines three made-up outcome distributions for a typical, attacking and blocking over.
sections.why: Gives the tests fixed inputs whose correct answers are easy to reason about.

sections.name: option-conditioned win probability (options) (part 1)
sections.title: Shrinkage, windows and decisions
sections.what: Checks that shrinkage gives a weighted blend of counts and prior. Checks that an attacking option moves the win chance more than a blocking one within a window, and that a one-ball window moves it less than a full over. Checks the best option, the coin-flip band, insufficient data, weighted counts, and the band lookup. Checks that an option with no counts falls back to the prior and is marked insufficient.
sections.why: Likely reason: every number on a decision should be traceable to counts and a prior.
sections.watch_out: Zero counts give a zero total rather than an error. Callers must not assume a non-zero total.

sections.name: option-conditioned win probability (options) (part 2)
sections.title: Options offered by required rate
sections.what: Checks that the intent decision offers attack, hold and ease off when the required rate is in the right band. Checks that bands which do not exist are dropped, so only the sensible options remain.
sections.why: Likely reason: fans should only be offered choices that make sense for their situation.
sections.watch_out: The band thresholds are fixed in these tests. Changing the thresholds changes which options appear.

summary: Checks the option maths on synthetic distributions: shrinkage toward a prior, applying an option to a window of balls, choosing the best option with coin-flip and insufficient-data rules, counting outcomes, and offering options by required-rate band.
purpose: Proves the option maths before it is applied to real data.
why: Likely reason: the real results depend on this maths, so it is checked on known cases first.
how: Builds three made-up outcome distributions. Runs the decision and win-probability functions, checks shrinkage arithmetic, checks that an attacking option moves the win chance more than a blocking one, checks counts and bands, and checks which options are offered for each required-rate band.
inputs: Synthetic distributions and counts built inside the test.
risks: The band labels and cut points are fixed. Changing them changes the options fans see.
debug: If the options list fails, check the required-rate band logic. If decision tests fail, check the minimum sample and the coin-flip band used.
